picks.title: Poll finds 100% of Japanese online game developers are using AI, though mostly for 'user preference analysis' and 'user behavior prediction'
picks.excerpt: A Japan Online Game Association survey reports that every responding online game developer now uses AI somewhere in their pipeline, but overwhelmingly for player-preference analysis and behavior prediction rather than asset or content generation. It is a rare hard data point on where AI actually lands in production workflows versus where the discourse assumes it lands.
picks.rationale: Rare hard survey data showing AI adoption is near-total but concentrated in analytics, not asset generation - directly corrects the assumption driving most AI-in-games discourse.

picks.title: Build a mockup UI with Unity MCP
picks.excerpt: Unity shows how to connect an AI agent to the Unity MCP server and prompt it to generate a placeholder main menu with UI Toolkit, then wire up button logic by hand. It is a practical demo of MCP-driven agents doing greybox UI work that a team restyles later.
picks.rationale: The most directly actionable pick - a first-party, reproducible MCP-agent workflow a designer can run in the editor tomorrow for greybox UI.

picks.title: Modern Warfare 4 studio head on AI in game dev: 'We use whatever tools we can'
picks.excerpt: Infinity Ward's studio head takes a matter-of-fact line on AI in Modern Warfare 4's development, framing it as one more tool available to the team. It is a rare AAA-scale statement of AI as ordinary pipeline tooling rather than a strategic announcement.
picks.rationale: A AAA studio head treating AI as ordinary pipeline tooling - a normalization signal distinct from the vendor hype and the indie backlash already covered.

picks.title: New Viral Friendslop Game Criticized For Epstein Jokes And Generative AI
picks.excerpt: Viral co-op title Dear Passengers is drawing backlash over both its humor and its use of generative AI assets, showing how quickly the 'friendslop' genre's fast production cadence collides with player scrutiny. It is a live case of AI-accelerated content shipping ahead of its own art direction.
picks.rationale: A live case of a hit shipping AI assets ahead of its own art direction and paying for it in player scrutiny - the reputational cost of speed.

picks.title: It seems like engineers are vibe coding game ports with access to the source code
picks.excerpt: Google's AI Studio lead vibe-coded an iOS port of Command & Conquer using the released source code, reframing LLM-assisted porting as a real engineering workflow rather than a toy demo. It sharpens the question of what 'vibe coding' means when the model is handed a legitimate codebase instead of a prompt.
picks.rationale: Vibe coding with a legitimate codebase in hand is a different engineering proposition than prompt-only ports - a concrete counterpoint to the recompilation-community story.
